# Salesforce Case alert suppression and rearming policy — concept pack

> Compare qualification transitions, per-status flags, recurring scheduling and feedback loops before choosing a shared Case-alert episode policy.

## Facets

- [Structure and components](llms-full.txt#structure-and-components): The Case-Flow discussion contains competing suppression designs: one participant proposes a highest-status field, while another warns that it suppresses a later visit to an earlier stage that was previously skipped. — 1 unit
- [How it works](llms-full.txt#how-it-works): With transition-only evaluation of an OR predicate, changing from one qualifying status to another does not create a new entry into the predicate.; Transition-only evaluation suppresses repeated matches: updates that leave a Case qualified should not send another alert.; For transition-based record-triggered Flow scheduled paths, an update that makes the record ineligible cancels pending paths; an unrelated update that preserves eligibility leaves existing paths scheduled. — 4 units
- [Comparisons and alternatives](llms-full.txt#comparisons-and-alternatives): In a firsthand Case-Flow discussion, the author reports that per-status checkboxes bypass a notification when a Case returns to a status whose notification was already sent.; A participant in that Case-Flow discussion proposes recording a date instead of a checkbox for each initial status update, so the same suppression marker can also support time-in-stage calculations.; Policy inference for an external Case alerter: treat continuous qualification as one alert episode and rearm after qualification becomes false and later true. — 4 units
- [Facts and statements](llms-full.txt#facts-and-statements): Salesforce documents suppressing repeat Case escalation emails on description-only edits by checking whether the status changed to Escalated.; Field-based scheduled paths have an important scope exception: moving the time source into the future while criteria are met can schedule execution again even after the path already ran. — 2 units
